## Design

### 2026-10-26: This week, I am going to make a small display unit that will show statistics about my Raspberry Pi and Oracle Cloud servers.

**1.47h**

This week, I am going to make a small display unit that will show statistics about my Raspberry Pi and Oracle Cloud servers.
It will run off USB-C, and refresh about every 5 minutes or so, using WiFi to fetch data.
Inspiration:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/477b7f4f9296c3b2d85b6f3bc4b4decebe961d735dc6187fe61ceb003ea5ac06.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/c40c6df64e2657d1dbbef2263370b34b7db8faf8bf648702c21a21839ad29c7c.png)

I therefore spent some time today planning and researching this.
The hardest and most time-consuming part was finding a display. They are really quite expensive, and the ones I wanted the most were just a few pounds over-budget. I eventually settled on this tiny little 2.15” e-paper panel:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/11d2efbb15523e8d345ee7afa12fe137411489156f564c8134663e8e7289fd32.png)
It’s smaller than I had initially hoped, but actually, that means it won’t take up too much space, which is good.
Powered by a Seeed Xiao EE04, which has an ESP32-S3 chip (faster than an RP2040!). This has all the driver stuff AND the processor, as well as some buttons, that I need.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/390d2939a12961e5746e1eafde94f295c8d60f75d6d1e32a0794013c445d3b08.png)
The buttons will let me switch between different pages, to see different stats, and/or stats for different servers.
I’ll program the interface in Python, and fetch data from the servers rather than the other way round.
I’ll 3D model a case for it, which I can 3D print after Half Life with the 3D printer I will hopefully earn!

### 2026-10-27: Okay, slight change of plan.

**2.63h**

Okay, slight change of plan.

I was doing some final research today before I committed to the specific hardware for this project, and I'm very glad I did. It turns out that this Seeed driver board was really designed for use with Seeed displays. Since Seeed has to be delivered to the UK from China at a very high cost, I really want to stick with UK-based retailers since the hardware for this project is expensive already. Plus, it was really designed to be a no-code platform with a GUI to customise and display stuff. So it wouldn't be a particularly smooth experience getting it all working. I'm talking custom drivers, hand-written LUTs, etc.

So, I have changed my hardware plan. Instead of the Seeed board, I'm going with a (cheaper) Pi Pico WH. I'll be pairing that with a pi-pico compatible Waveshare 2.13" ePaper display, which has all the driver stuff built in and is designed specifically for the Pi Pico.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/d15ebe6dcb57a5d0bfdb59b4bb0957783ffb36c9db16360e563d4d395d1e8956.png)

With this decided (and it actually fits better within my budget, which is great. And the screen and pi are well in stock so hopefully still will be by the time I buy them [the other stuff was low on stock]), I moved onto 3D modelling an enclosure, which I will 3D print with the printer I hopefully get from this event. The model is as accurate as I can be without the real hardware, so once I get the real stuff, I'll update the measurements. the enclosure looks pretty cool, though!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/371b74f3128697d5225d5b08de43a556283e452f7976456e6c003ec52eb4bc1c.png)

Finally, I researched and planned how the software is going to work. This is a much more software-heavy project this week, which is a nice change of pace, and exciting since I love programming. I will use MicroPython on the Pi, and Python on the server(s) to report the stats. So far, I have started writing the code to collect all the system resource data using psutil, and roughly planned out the program flow and logic. And, of course, I'm writing it to be clean and as modular and object-oriented as possible.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/EBuChAcUkspX5zhs3qEVPUNL9stbHepB/24044237aeb91da84e5d56199b3875b9381cf878be56eb836fb2ecd4731a518a.png)

Super excited to keep working tomorrow!

### 2026-10-28: PROGRAMMING PROGRAMMING PROGRAMMING

**1.2h**

PROGRAMMING PROGRAMMING PROGRAMMING

That's what I've been doing today. Still working on the server-side stats reporting code.
Specifically, I've been working on formatting the raw data received from psutil. I'm using lots of f-strings to format it into a nice string per datum, so when it comes to sending the data, it is already formatted. This means that when the Pi Pico receives the data, all it will have to do is display what it's been given, with essentially no formatting required. Not that string formatting is too intensive, but every optimisation I can make is a good thing!

I reckon another couple of hours of coding, and I'll have the server-side code all done. Then, I can work on the MicroPython code for receiving the data (probably the hardest part), and figure out roughly how the display code will work, too, although I might not be able to get super far without the hardware.

### 2026-10-29: Stats code is all done!

**1h**

Stats code is all done!

Today, I have finished all the code to format the stats received from psutil, and dump it into a nice json file. The idea is that access to this file will be opened up to the pi pico, using some security. Possibly a daily cryotpgraphic token that is needed to make the connection. I'll use a very barebones flask server to open access to this file, and the pi pico can request the json file every 5 minutes via http.

So now all I need to do is get the server code ready to run every 5 mins (or at whatever offset feels sensible so it doesn't collide with the pico's requests), and dump it into the json file, overwriting it. Then write the code for the pico to receive it!

### 2026-10-30: Programming is going so well!

**2.2h**

Programming is going so well!

Today, I have made some huge progress. I got the client and server talking properly, and managed to send the stats data across 2 different devices on my network with 100% consistency. I hooked up the stats fetching code into a main loop that can be run on the server, using a lightweight flask app to open up access to the json file. The code will work on both my raspberry pi (local network so no issues there) and my oracle server (i can probably just open the port, or maybe set up tailscale or something but probably just open the port lol).

Then I moved on to the client code. With the receiving code already written, I made this into a module I could import, and started writing the client loop. I will run it as a loop in a constant process instead of a cron job so that way the display can retry if requesting data fails for some reason. I then began working on parsing the incoming data and pulling out the pre-formatted data that I want for each page.

I have also started thinking about how I will render the info. For now, I will do it through a temporary class that renders it to my terminal. When I come to make it work on the pi pico, I will write an equivalent class that uses the same methods externally but renders to the ePaper display. That way none of the main code has to change!

### 2026-10-31: Programming is essentially done!

**2h**

Programming is essentially done!

I've been super busy today. First, I finished up the page layouts, deciding what data would go on which page. After a lot of formatting and tidying up, I have decided on a layout system.

I then loaded the server code onto my real Oracle server, and tested it! It crashed, but all I had to do was add some checks for if data had been received, and add a fallback if not. I got it all working, but then the Minecraft server stat detection didn't work. I therefore fixed this code to not only filter by tmux session name, but also to filter by the java command to get the process information of the Minecraft server process. Since the server.jar files have different names for the 2 servers I host, it's super simple to work out which is which and get the stats for it.

Finally, I converted the code over to MicroPython-compatible code (hopefully). So once I have the hardware, I can swap out the rendering class and it should be all good!

(Note I've just included images of the python, not micropython code because it looks nicer and tidier.)

### 2026-11-01: The project is done!

**1h**

The project is done!

Today I went through the code and fixed all of the bugs. I also made it more secure by removing any hard-coded IP addresses or secret tokens, loading these from separate files instead. Although the contents of these files is of course still visible, it means that the code I upload to my GitHub does not have any secret information in it.

I also made the secret token system more secure. Now instead of a plain text token, a daily token is created. This hashes a combination of a secret string and the current date. This should make it more secure.

So the project is done! Super excited to build this one! It's gonna be awesome.
